sentences.text: Claimants being parents of deceased Durgesh Chauhan have filed application under section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act seeking compensation for death of their son in a motor vehicle accident.
Background 2.
Succinctly stated, Durgesh Chauhan along with his friends was travelling in Innova Car from his Hostel, V.N.I.T. Campus, Nagpur to Pench National Park, Nagpur on 08.01.2017 at around 4:34 am.

As they reached near Sharda Company Chowk, Kamathi Road, one Truck bearing No.GJ-05-BX-1822 coming from the side of Kalamna Road at very high speed in rash and negligent manner hit their car causing serious injuries to its occupants whereas driver of the Car Nilesh Adinath Ramteke and deceased Durgesh Chauhan succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the accident and died at the spot.

sentences.text: 18. Certified copy of Criminal Record has been adduced in evidence as Ex.PW-3/2 and it is well settled law that negligence of driver in cases under Motor Vehicle Act is required to be proved on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt does not apply to claim petitions under Motor Vehicle Act as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 15 of Bimla Devi & Ors.

Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SCC 530.
19.
Following observations in para 15 of aforesaid judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court being relevant are extracted herein below :
"15. In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a praticular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimaints were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.

The standard MACT No. 185/2017 Mithlesh Kumari &
Anr. Vs. Raman Yadav & Ors. Page No. 7 of 20 of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied...."

20. Similar observation has been recorded by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 12 of its judgment delivered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2007 SCC Online Del 1700 holding that proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceeding in a civil suit hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed and FIR against the driver along with criminal record of the case showing completion of investigation by the police leading to Final Report are sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
21. Death of Durgesh Chauhan due to injuries sustained in motor vehicle accident is established from postmortem report of deceased mentioning 'Head Injury' as probable cause of death.
22. FINDING : Issue No.1 is therefore decided in favour of claimants by holding that Durgesh Chauhan has died due to fatal injuries in motor vehicle accident caused due to rash or negligent driving of Truck No. GJ-05BX-1822 by respondent No.1/Raman Yadav which vehicle was registered in the name of respondent No. 2/M/s Ritco Logistics Pvt. Ltd. and insured with respondent No.
3/United India Insurance Co. Ltd.

30. Since monthly income of Durgesh Chauhan as per Revised Salary effective from 01.04.2016 was Rs.40,536/- so 'Gross Annual Income' of deceased in the year 2016 is calculated as Rs.40,536 x 12 =
Rs.4,86,432/-.
A sum of Rs.2,50,000/- out of Rs.4,86,432/- was exempt from income tax in the year 2016 so income tax @ 10% on balance Rs.2,36,432/- (Rs.4,86,432 - Rs.2,50,000) would amount to Rs.23,643.20/-.
31. Net Annual Income Rs.4,62,788.80/- would be left with Durgesh Chauhan after deducting Rs.23,643.20/- from his Gross Annual Income Rs.4,86,432/- of the relevant year.

17. Hon'ble Punjab & Haryana High Court in Bimla Devi Vs. Punjab State, 2001 (1) RCR (Civil) 596 SC has held that statement of witness cannot be discarded simply because the witness did not report the matter to the police.
18. Certified copy of Criminal Record has been adduced in evidence as Ex.PW-3/2 and it is well settled law that negligence of driver in cases under Motor Vehicle Act is required to be proved on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt does not apply to claim petitions under Motor Vehicle Act as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 15 of Bimla Devi & Ors.
20. Similar observation has been recorded by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 12 of its judgment delivered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2007 SCC Online Del 1700 holding that proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceeding in a civil suit hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed and FIR against the driver along with criminal record of the case showing completion of investigation by the police leading to Final Report are sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
21. Death of Durgesh Chauhan due to injuries sustained in motor vehicle accident is established from postmortem report of deceased mentioning 'Head Injury' as probable cause of death.
22. FINDING : Issue No.1 is therefore decided in favour of claimants by holding that Durgesh Chauhan has died due to fatal injuries in motor vehicle accident caused due to rash or negligent driving of Truck No. GJ-05BX-1822 by respondent No.1/Raman Yadav which vehicle was registered in the name of respondent No. 2/M/s Ritco Logistics Pvt.
